newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bonn stands by 2.9 pct deficit projection - Stark.
newsitem.headline: Bonn stands by 2.9 pct deficit projection - Stark.

text.p: The German finance ministry stands by its projection of a public sector deficit of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product this year, believing it reflects all foreseeable negative scenarios, state secretary for finance Juergen Stark said on Monday.

Bonn revised the figure upward in January from an earlier projection of 2.5 percent, to a level that leaves little margin for error before reaching the 3.0 percent of GDP deficit ceiling required for participation in European monetary union.

"The 2.9 percent (deficit projection) ... is a carefully calculated figure, in which we have already considered all recognisable risks," Stark told journalists following a meeting of European finance ministers where he took the place of Finance Minister Theo Waigel.

The figure reflects a 0.3 percentage point downward revision in the government's projection of 1997 nominal GDP growth, made between November and January, and the possibility that the sluggish economy will again diminish tax revenues this year, he said. It also reflects an expected increase of 200,000 in average unemployment this year.

"The sharp increase in January unemployment is still far from posing a threat to this 2.9 percent figure," Stark said, but added he expects the January figure to prove to be a blip, reflecting the severe winter and other temporary and exceptional factors.

While the political decision whether to freeze budget outlays this year has not yet been reached, Stark said, it is clear that if tax revenues fall short of budgeted levels, that further corrective measures will be taken on the spending side.
Germany's progress in meeting the Maastricht convergence criteria is likely to be a central topic of the next EU finance ministers' meeting in March, he said.
